$schema-note: Image provenance manifest for images DERIVED from retained schematic PDFs by local rasterisation. Kept separate from media/manifest.json so that no pre-existing file is modified; an index owner may merge them.
global_notes: These are NOT photographs and NOT vendor-published images. Each is a crop of a page the vendor published as a vector PDF, rasterised locally at 300 dpi.

pdfimages could not be used: pdfimages -list reports ZERO embedded rasters in every source PDF here. The drawings are vector, so pdftoppm plus a crop is the only route. This is recorded because reaching for pdfimages is the obvious wrong first move.

Copyright in the underlying drawing remains with the vendor named in creator_rightsholder. Licence is UNKNOWN: no licence statement appears in any of the source PDFs. Redistribution status unknown; disposition repository, unstaged pending user review.
Every image is reproducible byte-for-byte from the retained artifact using the recorded generation_command, so none of them is uniquely held here.
Each image exists because it settles a specific documented question; see why_retained.

images.caption: Schematic crop: rotary encoder connector J5, five pins
images.alt_text: Schematic detail of a yellow symbol J5 captioned 'Rotary encode'. The upper half shows a switch contact between pins labelled b1 and b2, pin 1 going left to net BTN and pin 2 right to GND. The lower half shows three pins labelled A, COM and B, numbered 3, 4 and 5, with A and B dropping to nets IN_A and IN_B and 10 kilohm pull-ups R2 and R3, and COM going to GND.
images.why_retained: Corrects the recorded seven-pad reading: the symbol has five pins. Establishes the topology as a three-terminal quadrature encoder with common grounded plus an integrated push switch.

images.caption: Schematic crop: buzzer LS1 and its drive circuit
images.alt_text: Schematic detail showing a buzzer symbol LS1 captioned 'Buzzer' with diode D6 1N4148WT drawn anti-parallel across it, both between the supply rail and the collector of transistor Q5, an SS8050 NPN. The base path runs from net beep through resistor R25 470 ohm and then through capacitor C27 10 microfarad in series, with diode D7 1N4148WT clamping the base node to ground.
images.why_retained: Shows C27 is a series coupling capacitor in the base path rather than bulk decoupling, and shows D6 as a flyback catch diode, which establishes the transducer as inductive (magnetic) rather than piezo.
